stops.name: Bioi
stops.riddle:
They sell you no trinket, no treat and no tea,
just rooms not yet built that they already see.
With rulers and pencils they dream up a place,
then hammer it up into real living space.
clues: Nothing here goes home in a shopping bag - it's a studio where houses are designed and then actually built.
Far east end of the strip, the 1200 block of 9 Ave SE, on the north side (the Bow River side), past 12 Street.
Look for a short four-letter name in lowercase letters at number 1226A.
stops.challenge: Sketch or photograph the most interesting window or doorway on this block.

stops.name: Rain Dog Bar
stops.riddle:
Take the middle of doors, then climb up a flight,
where craft beer and wine keep good company at night.
Small plates out of Europe, perogies and cheer,
a hideaway perched up above the street here.
clues: A drinks-first spot famous for craft beer, with a wine list for everyone else, plus European-style small plates.
East end of the strip, the 1200 block of 9 Ave SE, north side, right next to the all-day brunch place at 1212.
You can't walk straight in - it's up a staircase behind the middle of three doors at 1214B, and the name is a wet, lost pup.
stops.challenge: Photograph the staircase door from the sidewalk and count the second-floor windows.

stops.name: Fair's Fair (For Book Lovers)
stops.riddle:
Shelves upon shelves of the pages of old,
where a story once read can be bought and resold.
Bring in your finished ones, trade for some more,
the river-end block hides this well-loved door.
clues: Paper, spines and second chances - a shop for people who read a lot and re-read even more.
West end of the strip, the 900 block of 9 Ave SE, south side, closest to the Fort Calgary and Bow River end.
It's unit L at number 907, and both words of the name start with the letter F.
stops.challenge: Find the tallest book on any shelf and photograph it next to your hand for scale.

stops.name: Tuu Shop
stops.riddle:
Bracelets and blouses and bags on a hook,
a gathered-up collection wherever you look.
Small pretty things from all over to wear,
the west end of nine keeps this little place there.
clues: A small boutique stocking jewellery, clothing, accessories and gifts collected from all over the world.
West end of the strip, the 900 block of 9 Ave SE, north side, in unit 103 of the building at 902.
The first word of the name is only three letters long and starts with T.
stops.challenge: Spot something in the window that travelled from another country and photograph it.

stops.name: Two Wheel View
stops.riddle:
A pair of round rims with a chain in between,
fixed up by young hands still learning the scene.
Pay what you can, then go rolling away,
the west end of nine sends you off on your way.
clues: Not only a store - it's a charity where teenagers learn to fix the things that roll.
West end of the strip, the 900 block of 9 Ave SE, south side - same address as the big used-book shop, one unit over.
It's unit M at 907, and the name starts with a number spelled out as a word.
stops.challenge: Count the bikes you can see from the doorway and photograph the smallest one.

stops.name: Sweet Treats Co.
stops.riddle:
Cold in a cone or a cup if you please,
in flavours invented to make your brain freeze.
Pick out a topping or maybe pick two,
the eleven-hundred block is waiting for you.
clues: Something cold and scooped, best on a hot Calgary afternoon.
Middle of the strip, the 1100 block of 9 Ave SE, south side.
Three words on the sign, and the first one is another way of saying sugary.
stops.challenge: Photograph the flavour with the strangest name on the board.

stops.name: Next Page (The)
stops.riddle:
New ones up top and the old ones below,
with ladders that slide where the tall shelves go.
An espresso to sip while you hunt for a read,
a hundred-year building is all that you need.
clues: Books on the main floor, more books downstairs, and coffee while you browse.
East end of the strip, the 1200 block of 9 Ave SE, south side, in a block of shops built back in 1912.
Look for rolling ladders on the bookshelves; the second word of the two-word name is something every book is full of.
stops.challenge: Find the oldest-looking book in the basement and photograph its spine.

stops.name: Lasa By Cara
stops.riddle:
Brunch with a twist from a far-away shore,
Philippine flavours are what's here in store.
Morning-time plates with a tropical flair,
the eleven-hundred block - go looking right there.
clues: A brunch spot mixing Filipino flavours with breakfast classics.
Middle of the strip, the 1100 block of 9 Ave SE, south side, just east of the ice cream shop.
The name is a short four-letter word starting with L, then the word 'by', then a woman's first name.
stops.challenge: Photograph the most colourful dish on the menu board.

stops.name: Oolong Tea House
stops.riddle:
Leaves in hot water left steeping a while,
in colour-coded tins all lined up in style.
Look up at the ceiling, pressed tin overhead,
skip past the coffee and sip green instead.
clues: No coffee needed here - the whole menu starts with leaves in hot water.
East end of the strip, the 1200 block of 9 Ave SE, south side, right beside the bookstore-with-a-coffee-bar.
The first word of the name is a type of tea, and the old ceiling inside is pressed tin.
stops.challenge: Photograph the tea with the most unusual name on the wall.

stops.name: Apothecary In Inglewood (The)
stops.riddle:
Jars full of botanicals, powders and oils,
bring your own bottle and cut down on spoils.
No prescriptions in here, just good scents in the air,
the west end of nine is where you'll find it there.
clues: Herbs, natural body care and refills - a low-waste wellness shop, and definitely not a pharmacy.
West end of the strip, the 900 block of 9 Ave SE, south side, a few doors east of the big used-book shop.
The name is an old-fashioned word for a herbalist's shop, and it ends with the name of this very neighbourhood.
stops.challenge: Find the jar with the longest ingredient name on it and photograph the label.

stops.name: Naan Tale
stops.riddle:
Off the busy main strip, down a side street you go,
where flatbread comes puffed from a fire's hot glow.
Each curry's a chapter, each spice tells a part,
a story you eat from the very first start.
clues: An Indian kitchen where the bread is every bit as famous as the curry.
Not on 9 Ave at all - head south and west onto 8 Street SE, over toward the Ramsay side.
Two words: the first is a kind of Indian flatbread, and the second rhymes with 'pail'.
stops.challenge: Photograph the bread section of the menu and pick one you have never tried.

stops.name: Lily By Lyla
stops.riddle:
Gowns on a rack, floor-length and grand,
for weddings and grads and a dance-floor band.
Sequins and satin all shimmer inside,
the east end of nine, where the windows are wide.
clues: A shop where nearly everything on the rack is a dress meant for a very big day.
East end of the strip, the 1200 block of 9 Ave SE, south side, past 12 Street.
Both names in the sign start with the letter L, and the window is full of formal gowns.
stops.challenge: Photograph the sparkliest dress you can see in the window.

stops.name: Opulence Piercing
stops.riddle:
A tiny bright needle, a glint and a gleam,
then gold in your ear like a small shining beam.
Studs, hoops and gems in a case in a row,
mid-block on the avenue, that's where to go.
clues: You leave here wearing a little more jewellery than you arrived with - and it doesn't just slip off.
Middle of the strip, the 1100 block of 9 Ave SE, south side, right at the west end of that block.
The name is a fancy word meaning 'luxury', followed by exactly what they do to you.
stops.challenge: Photograph the shiniest piece of jewellery in the display case.

stops.name: Gallery Underground
stops.riddle:
Pictures on walls and some art that goes deeper,
ink under skin from a steady-armed keeper.
Step off the sidewalk and through the right door,
the west end of nine hides a hideaway floor.
clues: Half art space, half tattoo studio - two very different kinds of picture under one roof.
West end of the strip, the 900 block of 9 Ave SE, south side, in unit 10 at number 917.
Two words: the first is where paintings hang, and the second is what you call anything below the surface.
stops.challenge: Ask first, then photograph your favourite artwork on the wall.

stops.name: Madison's 12|12
stops.riddle:
All-day-long breakfast and bowls piled high,
a big heated patio open to sky.
Bring your laptop and coffee or come with a crowd,
the east end of nine, where the brunch line is loud.
clues: Brunch served all day, plus nachos and bowls, and a patio people happily camp out on.
East end of the strip, the 1200 block of 9 Ave SE, north side, right where the block begins.
The sign splits the street number in half and repeats it with a bar between the two halves.
stops.challenge: Count the tables on the patio and photograph the busiest one.

stops.name: Adorn Boutique
stops.riddle:
Dresses for weddings and grads and for guests,
with jewellery and shoes to go with the rest.
A family picks every piece with great care,
the east end of nine - you won't miss it there.
clues: A women's clothing boutique especially known for dresses for special occasions.
East end of the strip, the 1200 block of 9 Ave SE, north side, a couple of doors from the brunch spot at 1212.
One word, starting with A, and it means to decorate or dress yourself up.
stops.challenge: Find the dress in the window with the most sparkle and photograph it.

stops.name: Nash Restaurant (The)
stops.riddle:
A hotel from long ago wears a brand-new name,
where a wood-smoke rotisserie turns for its fame.
Round the corner from nine, on a street heading down,
you'll find one of the handsomest rooms in this town.
clues: Dinner in a heritage building, best known for chicken turned slowly over wood smoke, with a small cocktail lounge attached.
Just off the main strip - turn south onto 11 Street SE from 9 Ave.
It lives inside the restored National Hotel, and its own name is four letters starting with N.
stops.challenge: Photograph the oldest-looking part of the building - old brick, an old sign, or an old window.

stops.name: Curated Home (The)
stops.riddle:
Cushions and lamps and a chair you could keep,
vases and blankets to curl up and sleep.
Nothing to eat and no clothes you can wear,
just beautiful things for a room somewhere.
clues: Everything inside belongs in a living room or a bedroom, not on you.
Between the two ends of the strip, the 1000 block of 9 Ave SE, north side, just east of the 900s.
Three words beginning with 'The', and the last word is the place where you live.
stops.challenge: Find the softest thing in the store and photograph it.

stops.name: Chin Whiskey
stops.riddle:
Hot towels and clippers and straight-razor steel,
where a beard gets a tidy and cheeks get to feel.
Just off the main strip, down a quieter street,
walk in a bit shaggy, walk out looking neat.
clues: A proper old-school barbershop: haircuts, beard trims and hot-towel shaves.
Off 9 Ave - head south down 11 Street SE, close to the restaurant in the old hotel.
The two-word name sounds like a drink you'd pour, but the first word is a part of your face.
stops.challenge: Photograph the barber pole or the shelf of shaving and beard products.

stops.name: Pronto Pizza
stops.riddle:
Round as a moon and then cut into eight,
With cheese pulling long from the box to the plate.
No knife and no fork — you just fold up a slice,
Hot from the oven and gone in a trice.
clues: This one is all about dough, sauce and cheese — you can usually smell the oven before you find the door.
The 1100 block of 9th Avenue SE, south side, right in the middle of the strip — look for a numbered bay tucked into the building rather than a corner spot.
The name is the Italian word for 'quick', and it starts with P.
stops.challenge: Photograph the menu and count how many different toppings you could choose from, then pick your dream three.

stops.name: Stash
stops.riddle:
A rainbow of bundles all wound into balls,
Soft little towers stacked high on the walls.
Two pointy sticks, then a loop and a twist —
A scarf can appear from a flick of the wrist.
clues: Knitters and crocheters treat this place like a clubhouse; everything sold here is soft and comes in colours.
Far east end, the 1200 block of 9th Avenue SE, south side of the street — one of the last shops before the strip runs out.
Five letters, meaning a secret hoard you keep tucked away, starting with S — and the sign calls itself a 'lounge'.
stops.challenge: Find the fuzziest yarn in the shop and take a photo of the colour you would pick for a hat.

stops.name: Murphy's Mid-Century
stops.riddle:
Skinny wood legs from your grandparents' day,
Low wooden sideboards and sofas in grey.
Nineteen-sixty is still living here,
Where old-fashioned somehow looks new every year.
clues: Furniture, but not new furniture — think tapered wooden legs and the shapes your grandparents' living room had.
East end, the 1200 block of 9th Avenue SE, south side, in a lettered unit squeezed between neighbours.
It is named after someone with a very Irish surname starting with M, followed by the hundred-year span it sells from.
stops.challenge: Spot a chair with tapered wooden legs and photograph it from floor level, looking up.

stops.name: Dragon Pearl
stops.riddle:
A serpent of legend curls through the name,
Chasing a gem in a moonlit old game.
But the treasure in here isn't silver or gold —
It's noodles and rice, and it's never served cold.
clues: Chinese cooking, both sit-down and takeout — the kind of place that has been feeding this block a long while.
East end, the 1200 block of 9th Avenue SE, south side, in the same tight row as the pizza place and the vintage furniture shop.
Two words: a mythical flying creature, then the gem that grows inside an oyster. It starts with D.
stops.challenge: Take a photo of the item on the menu with the longest name, then try to say it in one breath.

stops.name: Gravity Espresso And Wine Bar
stops.riddle:
By day it's a bean that is ground up and pressed,
By night it's a glass with a swirl and a rest.
Its name is the pull that makes apples fall down —
One of the coziest corners in town.
clues: Two drinks under one roof: something hot and caffeinated in the morning, something poured from a bottle at night.
Not on the main avenue — it's around the corner on 10th Street SE, at the west end of the district, a few steps off 9th.
Named for the invisible force that pulls everything toward the ground. It starts with G.
stops.challenge: Photograph the drinks board and count how many items on it you cannot pronounce.

stops.name: Deane House
stops.riddle:
A century-old home with a porch and a stair
Was somebody's address; now dinner is there.
It sits by the Elbow, where currents run cold,
Across from the fort where this city took hold.
clues: A restaurant and bar where the building itself is the main attraction — it is older than almost everything around it.
The very west end: the 800 block of 9th Avenue SE, right where the road crosses the Elbow River, directly opposite the Fort Calgary grounds.
Two words — the surname of an early North-West Mounted Police superintendent, then the word for a building people live in. It starts with D.
stops.challenge: Photograph the front porch from the sidewalk, then find a heritage plaque nearby and note the year on it.

stops.name: Inglewood Pizza & Pasta
stops.riddle:
Two Italian cousins share one little shop:
The first is a circle with cheese on the top,
The second, long ribbons that twirl on a fork —
Order them both if you've done a day's work.
clues: Italian comfort food of the delivery-box kind, and both of the classic dishes are right there in the name.
East end, the 1200 block of 9th Avenue SE, south side, in a lettered unit in the row of small storefronts.
The first word of the name is the name of this entire neighbourhood. It starts with I.
stops.challenge: Photograph the largest pizza size on the menu and work out how many slices each person in your group would get.

stops.name: Moonstone Creation
stops.riddle:
Bead upon bead, sewn slow and by hand,
Makes flowers and stars you can wear on a band.
The art here is Indigenous, careful and true,
And the stone in the name shines a pale milky blue.
clues: A gallery and gift shop of Indigenous art — look for beadwork, leather and jewellery rather than paintings on white walls.
Not on the main avenue: one block south, in the 1200 block of 10th Avenue SE, at the east end of the district.
Its name pairs a milky-white gemstone named for the night sky with a word meaning 'something made'. It starts with M.
stops.challenge: Find a beaded piece and photograph it up close, then count how many beads fit in a square the size of your thumbnail.

stops.name: Bussin
stops.riddle:
A patty, a bun and a shake thick as glue,
Plus waffles with squares you can poke a thumb through.
The name is a word that the young people say
When something tastes so good it makes their whole day.
clues: Burgers, shakes and waffles — the sort of order that needs two hands and a stack of napkins.
The 1100 block of 9th Avenue SE, south side, in the middle stretch of the strip.
Six letters of modern slang meaning 'unbelievably delicious'. It starts with B.
stops.challenge: Take a photo of the tallest milkshake you can spot and guess how many scoops went into it.

stops.name: Kups
stops.riddle:
Street food from Korea, both spicy and sweet,
Served fast from a unit just off the main street.
Its name is a word for a thing that holds tea,
But the letter it starts with is wrong — you'll soon see.
clues: Korean street food: quick, bold and built to be eaten standing up.
West end, the 1000 block of 9th Avenue SE, north side — a numbered unit inside one of the newer buildings, not an old brick storefront.
Four letters, sounds exactly like the plural of the thing you drink coffee from, but it begins with K.
stops.challenge: Photograph the spiciest thing on the menu and dare a friend to say its name out loud.

stops.name: F45 Inglewood
stops.riddle:
No shopping in here and there's nothing to eat,
Just burpees and music and thump-thumping feet.
The whole thing is timed — forty-five on the dot —
Then out to the sidewalk, exhausted and hot.
clues: Nobody here is buying anything or eating anything; they came to sweat in a group, all doing the same move at once.
West end, the 1000 block of 9th Avenue SE, north side — a numbered unit in the same newer building as a small Korean spot.
A single letter followed by a two-digit number, and that number is how many minutes a class lasts. The letter is F.
stops.challenge: Take a polite photo from the sidewalk and count how many people are doing the exact same move at the same moment.

stops.name: Sot
stops.riddle:
Three letters only — the name's very short,
But the flavours inside are the fiery sort.
Korea, reworked with a chef's clever hand,
One of the newest arrivals to land.
clues: Korean cooking, but the sit-down, book-a-table kind rather than the grab-it-and-go kind.
East end, the 1200 block of 9th Avenue SE, north side, in a lettered unit facing the little shops across the road.
The shortest business name on the whole street: three letters, rhymes with 'pot', and it starts with S.
stops.challenge: Find the shortest business name on this block and photograph its sign.

stops.name: Marshall Drugs
stops.riddle:
A counter out back where prescriptions get filled,
With shelves full of remedies, bottled and pilled.
But here is the surprise in this old corner store:
Your letters and parcels head out through the door.
clues: If you had a cough, this is where a grown-up would take you — and you can send mail while you wait.
Far east end, the 1200 block of 9th Avenue SE, south side, only a couple of doors along from the yarn shop.
A person's surname followed by an old-fashioned word for medicines. It starts with M.
stops.challenge: Find and photograph the strangest flavour of cough drop or lozenge on the shelf.

stops.name: Limitless Calgary
stops.riddle:
Sofas and tables and chairs in a row,
All modern in shape from their tops to below.
The name is a promise that there is no end —
No stopping, no ceiling, no edge to defend.
clues: Everything inside is something you would sit on, eat at or sleep in, and all of it looks like it stepped out of a design magazine.
West end, the 1000 block of 9th Avenue SE, south side, close to the Italian market.
One word meaning 'without any boundary at all', followed by the name of this city. It starts with L.
stops.challenge: Photograph the chair you would most want in your bedroom, and the one you would least want.

stops.name: Hello Vintage Inglewood
stops.riddle:
Clothes with a history, worn once before,
Denim and dresses from decades of yore.
The name is a greeting you'd say with a wave,
Then a word for the old but still fashionably brave.
clues: Clothing, but nothing here is new — every single piece was already somebody else's favourite.
East end, the 1200 block of 9th Avenue SE, north side, in a lettered unit roughly across from the drugstore.
The first word is the friendliest thing you can say to a stranger. It starts with H.
stops.challenge: Find the oldest-looking garment in the shop and photograph its label.

stops.name: Haunted Objects
stops.riddle:
The name sounds like something from midnight and mist,
A shop where a shiver runs right up your wrist.
Whatever's inside, it's the words on the sign
That give you the goosebumps — spooky by design.
clues: A shop whose name belongs in a ghost story — the sort of doorway you would dare a friend to walk through.
Not on the main avenue: one block south, in the 1200 block of 10th Avenue SE, at the east end of the district.
Two words — the first means 'visited by ghosts', the second simply means 'things'. It starts with H.
stops.challenge: Photograph the spookiest-looking thing you can find nearby and invent a name for it.

stops.name: Linas Italian Piazza
stops.riddle:
Olive oil, pasta and coffee to go,
Imported from Italy, row upon row.
The last word means 'square' — not the shape, but the town
Kind, where the neighbours all stroll up and down.
clues: Part grocery shop, part cafe, and nearly everything on the shelves comes from one country shaped like a boot.
West end, the 1000 block of 9th Avenue SE, south side, a couple of doors from the modern furniture store.
A woman's first name with an apostrophe-S, then the country, then the Italian word for a town square. It starts with L.
stops.challenge: Photograph the most unusual pasta shape you can find and try to pronounce its name.

stops.name: Mowgli's/Ninja Tiger
stops.riddle:
A boy from a jungle, a cat with black stripes —
Two names at one address, of two different types.
The kitchen sends out something fragrant and spiced,
With warm bread for scooping and mountains of rice.
clues: Indian cooking — the kind of smell that reaches the sidewalk well before you reach the door.
East end, the 1200 block of 9th Avenue SE, south side, near where the row of small storefronts begins.
One address, two names: a jungle boy from a famous storybook, and a striped big cat paired with a stealthy warrior. They start with M and N.
stops.challenge: Photograph a dish on the menu you have never heard of, then look up what is in it.

stops.name: Eden (The)
stops.riddle:
A garden from stories where everything grew,
With apples and orchards and mornings of dew.
But this one's a bistro with butter and cream,
And brunch on a plate like a Frenchman's best dream.
clues: A small bistro with a French accent to its cooking — think brunch, butter and something rich.
East end, the 1200 block of 9th Avenue SE, south side, right beside the mid-century furniture shop.
Named after the most famous garden in any storybook: four letters, starting with E, with 'The' in front.
stops.challenge: Take a photo of the most garden-like thing you can spot at this address — a plant, a flower, or a leaf on a plate.

stops.name: Potion Room
stops.riddle:
Wizards and witches both stop for a sip,
Where elixirs are stirred with a flourish and flip.
No cauldron of soup and no textbook of spells,
Just glassware that bubbles and curious smells.
clues: A grown-ups-only bar where the drinks are treated like enchanted brews rather than plain old cocktails.
East end of the strip, odd numbers on the south side of 9 Ave, in the 1200 block just past 12 Street.
Its name starts with P and rhymes with 'ocean' — followed by a word for a space you stand inside.
stops.challenge: Photograph the most magical-looking bottle or glass you can spot from the doorway.

stops.name: Espy
stops.riddle:
Racks full of denim and jackets to try,
A mirror that asks you, 'Well then? What'll you buy?'
Shoes in a row standing patient and neat,
All waiting on somebody's outfit and feet.
clues: Not a place to eat — a place to get dressed, with staff who will happily style you head to toe.
The west end of the strip, the 1000 block on the odd-numbered south side, close to the Fort Calgary and Bow River end of 9 Ave.
Four letters starting with E — an old-fashioned word meaning 'to catch sight of something'.
stops.challenge: Find the boldest pattern in the window display and take a photo of it.

stops.name: Genuine Design
stops.riddle:
The labels are fancy, the price tags are kind,
Each treasure was somebody's before.
A closetful of luxury given new life —
Step in through the second-hand door.
clues: A clothing shop where everything has had a previous owner, but every name on the label is a posh one.
East end, odd-numbered south side of the 1200 block of 9 Ave, just east of 12 Street.
Two words: the first means 'real, not fake' and starts with G; the second is what an artist does before making something.
stops.challenge: Spot a handbag in the window, guess what it cost when it was new, then check the tag if you dare.

stops.name: Ari Sushi
stops.riddle:
Rice rolled in seaweed, all tidy and tight,
With ginger and wasabi adding the bite.
Chopsticks stand waiting, the soy sauce is poured,
And fish from the ocean is what's on the board.
clues: A restaurant where a lot of the fish arrives cool and raw rather than fried.
Right at the corner where 12 Street meets 9 Ave, at the very start of the 1200 block on the south side.
A three-letter name starting with A, followed by the name of the food itself.
stops.challenge: Take a photo of the menu item with the longest name.

stops.name: Purr
stops.riddle:
Its name is the noise of a cat feeling grand,
Though no whiskers live here at all.
Just dresses and scarves and small sparkling things
Arranged for the shoppers who call.
clues: A boutique for clothing and accessories, with a name borrowed from a very contented animal.
Far east end, odd-numbered south side of 9 Ave, well into the 1200 block past 12 Street.
Four letters, starts with P, and it is exactly the sound a happy cat makes.
stops.challenge: Find something in the window a cat would love to sit on, and photograph it.

stops.name: Burn Block Social Club
stops.riddle:
Silver balls rattle and flippers go snap,
Lights start to flash and the bumpers fire back.
A cold glass of beer while a high score is chased,
Old-fashioned fun in a modern-day place.
clues: A 19+ hangout where the entertainment is coin-operated, flashing and gloriously noisy.
East end, odd-numbered south side of 9 Ave in the 1200 block — and look for the unit marked B.
Four words. The first is what a fire does, the second is a chunk of a street, and the last two describe a club you socialise in.
stops.challenge: Photograph the pinball machine with the most colourful artwork.

stops.name: Lemonceillo Home
stops.riddle:
Candles and cushions and things for a shelf,
A gift for a friend, or for you.
Nothing gets cooked and no haircut is given,
Just pretty things, tidy and new.
clues: A shop stuffed with decorations and gifts for making a house feel nicer.
East end of the strip, odd-numbered south side, the 1200 block of 9 Ave — unit B.
The name begins with a sour yellow fruit and ends with the word HOME.
stops.challenge: Find the smallest gift in the shop and photograph it next to your hand for scale.

stops.name: Junction 9 Wellbeing
stops.riddle:
Roll out a mat and breathe slowly and deep,
Then stretch till your fingertips rise.
No treadmills, no whistles, no scoreboard, no crowd,
Just balance, and calm, and closed eyes.
clues: Not a shop and not a cafe — somewhere people come to move, stretch and breathe.
The west end of 9 Ave, the 900 block on the odd-numbered south side, closest to Fort Calgary and the Bow River.
Its name is a word for the place where two roads meet, followed by the number of the avenue you're standing on.
stops.challenge: Strike your best balancing pose outside the door and get a photo of it.

stops.name: Hose & Hound Pub
stops.riddle:
Long ago sirens once wailed from this door,
Where engines stood waiting on call.
The trucks grew too big and moved off down the road,
So now pints get poured in the hall.
clues: A neighbourhood pub inside a very old building that once had a far more urgent job.
The 1000 block, even-numbered north side of 9 Ave, toward the west end of the strip.
Two words joined by an ampersand: the first is what firefighters spray water through, the second is a kind of dog.
stops.challenge: Photograph anything on the outside of the building that hints at its firefighting past.

stops.name: Red's In Ramsay
stops.riddle:
Comfort on plates and a mug full of steam,
A booth and a brunch is a very fine dream.
But look off the avenue, over the hill,
Where the neighbouring district is quieter still.
clues: A diner-style spot known for comfort food and long, lazy brunches.
This one isn't on 9 Ave at all — it sits on 8 Street SE, a short walk south into the neighbourhood next door to Inglewood.
The name starts with a colour-ish nickname beginning with R, then the word 'in', then the name of that very neighbourhood.
stops.challenge: Photograph the most breakfast-looking plate you can see through the window.

stops.name: Analog
stops.riddle:
Beans that get ground and then poured out as brown,
Steam on the milk with a swirl spinning down.
The name means 'not digital' — dials, not screens,
A slow kind of morning is just what it means.
clues: Somewhere to get caffeinated — part of a small local cafe family.
Middle of the strip, the 1100 block on the odd-numbered south side of 9 Ave, in unit 1.
Six letters starting with A — it is the opposite of the word 'digital'.
stops.challenge: Find something genuinely analog nearby — a clock with hands, a printed menu, a record — and photograph it.

stops.name: Recordland
stops.riddle:
Black circles stacked into towering rows,
Spin one around and the music still flows.
No streaming, no downloads, no playlist, no phone,
Just crates you can dig through and treasure to own.
clues: A shop for people who like their music in a form they can hold in both hands.
The 1200 block on the even-numbered north side of 9 Ave, toward the east end.
Two words squashed into one: the thing you play on a turntable, plus a word meaning 'a place'. It starts with R.
stops.challenge: Find the album with the strangest cover art and photograph it.

stops.name: Boft Fine Rugs Gallery
stops.riddle:
Knotted by hand in a faraway land,
With blossoms and borders and vines,
Unroll one out flat and a floor becomes art
In a gallery no painting defines.
clues: It calls itself a gallery, but what's on show belongs under your feet, not on the wall.
East end, odd-numbered south side, the 1200 block of 9 Ave — unit B.
A short four-letter name starting with B, followed by the words 'Fine Rugs'.
stops.challenge: Photograph the rug with the most colours you can count in it.

stops.name: Evi Beauty
stops.riddle:
Bottles and jars for your cheeks and your chin,
Gentle and clean is the promise within.
No razors, no scissors, no clippers, no dye,
Just soft-scented things that are pleasing to try.
clues: A small boutique for skin and makeup, with everything kept on the natural, gentle side.
The 1000 block, even-numbered north side of 9 Ave, out toward the west end near Fort Calgary.
A three-letter name starting with E, followed by a word meaning loveliness.
stops.challenge: Find the prettiest bottle in the window and photograph it.

stops.name: Mumbai Bites- Progressive Indian Cuisine
stops.riddle:
Chutneys get stirred and the spices get warm,
Street snacks arrive on a plate.
They come from a huge seaside Indian city —
All crunchy and tangy and great.
clues: An Indian restaurant that leans hard on the street-food style of one particular enormous coastal city.
The 1200 block, even-numbered north side of 9 Ave, unit C, near the east end.
The first word is India's biggest seaside city; the second is what you take with your teeth.
stops.challenge: Photograph the menu item with the most ingredients listed.

stops.name: Marshall's Rx Centre
stops.riddle:
When you're sniffly and sneezy and feeling unwell,
This counter is where you should go.
Small paper bags with your name printed on,
And advice from the person who'd know.
clues: Not a browsing sort of shop — it's where prescriptions get filled.
The very far east end of the strip, odd-numbered south side of the 1200 block, in a building with numbered suites — look for #214.
A person's surname starting with M, followed by 'Rx', the little symbol that means medicine.
stops.challenge: Find and photograph an Rx symbol somewhere on the building or its signage.

stops.name: 4Cats
stops.riddle:
Aprons go on and the paint jars come out,
A blank little canvas is waiting for you.
The name sounds like whiskers, but no pets are here,
Just brushes and colours brand new.
clues: A place where children make art — think aprons and paintbrushes, not paintings for sale.
The 1200 block, even-numbered north side of 9 Ave — unit B.
The name is a number stuck onto an animal: four of them, and they purr.
stops.challenge: Photograph the most colourful piece of kids' art you can see through the window.

stops.name: Onyx & Ivory Salon
stops.riddle:
Its name holds two colours as far apart
As midnight and moonlight can be.
Walk in with your hair looking one kind of way,
Walk out, take a look, and you'll see.
clues: Somewhere to get your hair done, named for two strongly contrasting colours.
The 1000 block, even-numbered north side of 9 Ave toward the west end — suite 116.
The first word is a black gemstone starting with O; the second is the creamy white of a tusk.
stops.challenge: Photograph the shop's sign and count how many colours are actually in it.

stops.name: Ironwood Stage And Grill
stops.riddle:
A stage at the back where the guitars get tuned,
A grill that keeps sizzling all night.
Its name is a timber that's famously hard —
Come early to grab a good sight.
clues: A 19+ venue where you can have dinner and hear a live band on the very same night.
The far east end, odd-numbered south side, deep in the 1200 block of 9 Ave.
Three parts: a very hard type of wood starting with I, then where performers stand, then 'and Grill'.
stops.challenge: Find a poster or listing for an upcoming show and photograph it.

stops.name: Patisseries Louise
stops.riddle:
Behind cool marble, under glass,
small towers of cream and berries pass.
A taste of Paris, east of the Bow —
the fanciest cakes need three days' notice, though.
clues: A French-style pastry counter — think tarts, layers and cream rather than muffins and drip coffee.
West end of the strip: the 1000 block of 9 Avenue SE, on the even-numbered (north) side, closest to the Fort Calgary end.
Individual pastries sit under glass on the front counter, and the name begins with P — the French word for a pastry shop.
stops.challenge: Photograph the prettiest pastry in the case without touching the glass.

stops.name: Wymbin
stops.riddle:
Leave your shoes beside the door,
find a mat upon the floor.
Breathe in slow and stretch up tall —
the quietest place along the wall.
clues: Not a shop at all — a calm studio where the only equipment is a mat and your own breath.
Farthest west on the hunt: the 900 block of 9 Avenue SE, a numbered unit inside a larger building near the Fort Calgary end.
Look for unit 50 and a short, unusual name starting with W; there are classes here for kids as well as grown-ups.
stops.challenge: Hold a tree pose on the sidewalk outside and get someone to photograph you at ten seconds.

stops.name: Artesano Galleria
stops.riddle:
Platters, pottery, lamps aglow,
kitchen treasures row on row.
The word out front means 'craftsman's hand' —
in unit B is where they stand.
clues: Home decor and kitchenware — the sort of place where a serving bowl counts as art.
East end: the 1200 block of 9 Avenue SE, on the odd-numbered (south) side, in unit B.
The first word is Spanish for 'artisan' and starts with an A; the shop also carries the Maison Berger fragrance-lamp line.
stops.challenge: Find the item in the window you'd least like to carry home on a bike, and photograph it.

stops.name: Be Brave
stops.riddle:
Threads of blue and gold are sewn
in patterns handed down through years.
A shirt can say what words cannot —
courage stitched in rows, not tears.
clues: A clothing showroom built around one country's embroidery tradition, not a Canadian label.
The 1000 block at the west end of 9 Avenue SE, even (north) side, a few doors east of the French pastry counter at 1002.
Blue-and-yellow branding and embroidered shirts called vyshyvanky; the two-word name begins with B and is an instruction to be courageous.
stops.challenge: Photograph the most intricate embroidery pattern you can spot from the sidewalk.

stops.name: Esker Foundation
stops.riddle:
Climb above the shops and street,
where the art is free to see.
Windows frame the downtown towers —
a ridge of glacial gravel names me.
clues: Contemporary art with changing exhibitions, and there's no admission charge.
Odd-numbered (south) side of the 1000 block of 9 Avenue SE — but don't look at street level; head up inside the brick art block.
The suite number 444 means the fourth floor, and the name starts with E: a geology word for a long ridge left behind by a glacier.
stops.challenge: From the top-floor windows, photograph the downtown skyline framed by the glass.

stops.name: Brooklyn Dumplings Shop
stops.riddle:
Little pockets, pinched and pleated,
steamed or fried and quickly eaten.
A New York borough lends its name
to something small that can't be beaten.
clues: A quick-serve spot built around one folded, filled little food.
Middle of the strip: the 1100 block of 9 Avenue SE, odd (south) side.
The name pairs a famous New York borough with the word 'dumpling' — look for the B.
stops.challenge: Count how many dumpling varieties are on the menu board, then photograph your count.

stops.name: Bored Brewing Company (The)
stops.riddle:
Behind the door, steel tanks stand tall,
hops and barley, that is all.
The name declares there's nought to do —
the taproom flatly proves that untrue.
clues: A craft brewery taproom — adults only, and what's poured is made on site.
East end: the 1200 block of 9 Avenue SE, upstairs in unit 200.
The name is a mood you'd never admit to on a Friday night, and it begins with B.
stops.challenge: Photograph the tap list and pick out the beer with the strangest name.

stops.name: Smithbilt Hats
stops.riddle:
Felt is steamed and shaped and pressed,
a brim curled up on either side.
The colour that a mayor gives away
is the crown this city wears with pride.
clues: A workshop where the headwear is actually made by hand, not just sold off a rack.
Step off the avenue for this one: it sits on 11 Street SE, a block south of the 9 Avenue shops.
This is the maker of Calgary's famous white cowboy hat; the name starts with S and ends with 'built' spelled the short way.
stops.challenge: Photograph a white hat — bonus points if someone is wearing it.

stops.name: T2722 Luxury Barista Experience
stops.riddle:
A letter and four digits make the sign,
no ordinary cup is poured.
Book a seat and watch the steam —
coffee treated as an art, adored.
clues: Coffee, but served as a booked experience rather than a grab-and-go line.
West end: the 1000 block of 9 Avenue SE, even (north) side, sharing a building with a French pastry counter.
The name is a code — a T followed by four numbers, echoing a Calgary postal code.
stops.challenge: Photograph the sign and work out what its numbers might stand for.

stops.name: Leo Boutique
stops.riddle:
Racks of labels, spare and clean,
shoes in rows on polished floor.
A lion's short name marks the spot
where the well-dressed come for more.
clues: A high-end fashion boutique carrying designer labels, footwear and accessories for men and women.
West end: the 1000 block of 9 Avenue SE, even (north) side, a couple of doors from the pastry shop at 1002.
Three letters, begins with L, and it doubles as the zodiac's lion.
stops.challenge: Find the most colourful pair of shoes in the window and photograph them.

stops.name: Inglewood Oak & Vine
stops.riddle:
A sturdy tree, a climbing plant —
the neighbourhood supplies the rest.
The shelves ignore the map entirely
and group by colour, shade and zest.
clues: A bottle shop where the stock is arranged by colour and flavour instead of by country.
Mid-strip: the 1100 block of 9 Avenue SE, odd (south) side.
The sign pairs the neighbourhood's own name with a tree and a climbing plant, joined by an ampersand.
stops.challenge: Photograph the sign and count how many words it takes to name the place.

stops.name: Made By Marcus
stops.riddle:
Cold and creamy, scooped up high,
small-batch flavours, always new.
Step one block south of all the fuss
and a walk-up window waits for you.
clues: Frozen treats made in small batches, with a flavour list that keeps changing.
Not on 9 Avenue at all — one block south, on 10 Avenue SE near 11 Street.
The name is literally 'made by' plus a person's first name, and that name starts with M.
stops.challenge: Photograph the flavour board, then pick the one flavour you'd never order.

stops.name: Doughnut Party
stops.riddle:
A ring of dough, a glossy top,
a box that's made for sharing round.
The second word means celebration —
sugar is the only sound.
clues: Sweet fried rings sold by the box, best eaten the same day you buy them.
Mid-strip: the 1100 block of 9 Avenue SE, odd (south) side, not far from the bottle shop at 1139.
Two words — the treat itself plus a word for a celebration; it starts with D, and the shop started out in Edmonton.
stops.challenge: Photograph the doughnut in the case with the most toppings on it.

stops.name: Respect Eyecare
stops.riddle:
Letters shrinking down a chart,
frames arranged along the wall.
They'll tell you if the world is blurred
and help you read the small.
clues: A health spot on the strip — the kind of place where you read letters out loud.
West end: the 1000 block of 9 Avenue SE, even (north) side, inside a building at unit 112.
Eyeglass frames on display, and the first word is a virtue you'd hope to be shown — it starts with R.
stops.challenge: Photograph the wildest pair of frames on display.

stops.name: Peacock Boutique Consignment
stops.riddle:
Someone else's finest dress
gets a second chance to shine.
A showy bird lends out its name
to feathers that were never mine.
clues: Clothing with a past — pre-loved fashion sold on behalf of its previous owners.
East end: the 1200 block of 9 Avenue SE, even (north) side, near the home-decor gallery at 1215.
The name is a bird famous for showing off its tail feathers, and it starts with P.
stops.challenge: Find the most colourful item on the rack nearest the door and photograph it.

stops.name: Apprentice Cafe And Bistro
stops.riddle:
Turn off the strip and down a lane,
past houses quiet as can be.
Coffee, a warm sandwich, ice cream —
and a skyline you can see.
clues: A very small café doing specialty coffee, breakfast sandwiches, and its own small-batch ice cream.
Not on 9 Avenue — duck onto one of the quiet residential avenues just south of the strip, toward the west end.
The name is what you call someone still learning a trade, and it starts with A.
stops.challenge: Photograph the view from the patio.

stops.name: 11-Eleven Liquor
stops.riddle:
One number says the same thing twice,
once in digits, once in letters.
Far east end where the avenue bends,
a cold shelf and nothing better.
clues: A bottle shop, adults only, right at the far end of the walk.
The far east end of 9 Avenue SE, the 1400 block, out past 14 Street.
The name repeats one number twice — first as digits, then spelled out in words.
stops.challenge: Photograph the sign and spot how the number is written two different ways.

stops.name: Delicious From Colombia
stops.riddle:
From a land of mountains, beans and rain,
a menu travels north to stay.
The name is really just a promise —
one word for tasty leads the way.
clues: A small restaurant serving the food of one South American country.
East end: the 1300 block of 9 Avenue SE, even (north) side, unit B, close to where the avenue reaches 14 Street.
The country in the name is Colombia, and the first word means 'very tasty' — it starts with D.
stops.challenge: Photograph a menu item you have never heard of before.

stops.name: Rosso Coffee Roasters Inglewood
stops.riddle:
An Italian word for red is on the cup,
the beans are roasted close to home.
Farthest east along the avenue,
the last warm stop before you roam.
clues: A local coffee roaster's café — beans first, everything else second.
The far east end: the 1400 block of 9 Avenue SE, sharing the corner with a bottle shop.
The name is the Italian word for the colour red, and it starts with R.
stops.challenge: Photograph the bag of beans from the most distant country of origin on the shelf.

stops.name: Minh Chau Vietnamese Restaurant
stops.riddle:
A steaming bowl arrives up front,
with noodles hiding underneath.
You'll need chopsticks and a spoon,
plus basil, lime, and bean sprout leaf.
clues: The specialty here is a fragrant noodle soup you eat with chopsticks and a spoon at the same time.
North side of 9 Avenue in the 1300 block, just east of the 13 Street SE corner, at number 1318.
The sign says which country's cuisine it serves, and the restaurant's own name starts with M.
stops.challenge: Photograph the menu item with the longest list of ingredients.

stops.name: Collector's Gallery (The)
stops.riddle:
The walls are hung with hills and skies,
with paint an artist's hand applies.
Step softly in and take a look;
each frame's a page from someone's book.
clues: Nothing here is edible or wearable. You come to look at what's on the walls, and maybe take one home.
North side of 9 Avenue at the far east end of the 1300 block, close to 14 Street SE, at number 1332.
It's an art space named after the people who buy the art, and it starts with C.
stops.challenge: Find a picture with water in it and photograph its title card (ask staff first).

stops.name: Monki Breakfast Club & Bistro
stops.riddle:
A morning crowd waits by the door
for eggs and coffee, cups and cream.
It calls itself a kind of club,
but all you need is appetite and dream.
clues: Brunch is the entire point here: eggs, coffee, and a weekend lineup.
Far east end, north side of 9 Avenue, Unit 4 in the big 1420 complex past 14 Street SE.
The cheeky name is a playful respelling of a jungle animal, and it starts with M.
stops.challenge: Take a photo of the brunch plate with the most colours on it.

stops.name: That Old Retro Store
stops.riddle:
Big wooden speakers, dials that glow,
a needle drops and starts to go.
The sound is warm, the gear is old;
here yesterday's machines are sold.
clues: If your grandparents' music machine quit working, this is where it would get fixed and where you'd find another one.
North side of 9 Avenue in the 1300 block, a couple of doors from the corner at 13 Street SE, at 1314A.
Turntables, records, and vintage stereo receivers fill the window, and the shop's name begins with T.
stops.challenge: Find the oldest year printed on any record sleeve or piece of gear and photograph it.

stops.name: Twitchin Threadz & Company
stops.riddle:
A wall of hangers, neatly hung,
with shirts and scarves for old and young.
Step inside and try a few;
the fit that fits is waiting for you.
clues: Clothing and accessories, picked out by a small crew who like to help you choose.
South side of 9 Avenue in the 1300 block, Unit 2 of the multi-unit building at 1335, shared with a barbershop.
The first word rhymes with 'itchin'' and the second word swaps an S for a Z; it starts with T.
stops.challenge: Photograph the loudest-patterned item in the whole shop.

stops.name: Tupi Acai Bowls
stops.riddle:
A purple berry, blitzed and cold,
in bowls with fruit piled on the top.
It travelled far from Brazil
to end up in this frosty shop.
clues: Frozen purple fruit served in a bowl, with gelato and smoothies on the side.
North side of 9 Avenue, far east end, first stretch of the 1400 block just past 14 Street SE, at number 1414.
Bright Brazilian fruit photos cover the menu board, and the name starts with T.
stops.challenge: Build or photograph a bowl with at least five different toppings.

stops.name: Boss Tattoos Walk - In Studio
stops.riddle:
No appointment? Wander in.
The artwork here goes on your skin.
A buzzing needle, steady hand,
and pictures that forever stand.
clues: The artists here draw on people instead of paper, and you don't have to book ahead.
South side of 9 Avenue in the 1300 block, number 1331, a few doors west of the 14 Street SE corner.
Flash art fills the window and the words 'walk-in' are on the sign; the name starts with B.
stops.challenge: Photograph the most colourful design in the window (looking only, no ink today).

stops.name: Foundation Barbershop
stops.riddle:
A spinning chair, a snap of cape,
a careful comb to set the shape.
The clippers hum, the hair drifts down,
and out you strut around the town.
clues: Walk in shaggy, walk out sharp. It's all about hair here.
South side of 9 Avenue in the 1300 block, Unit 3 at number 1335, right beside a clothing boutique.
Look for barbershop signage and clipper imagery; the name is a word for the base a building sits on, and starts with F.
stops.challenge: Count how many barber chairs there are, then photograph one (with permission).

stops.name: Nova Skin & Wellness
stops.riddle:
No haircut here, no cup of tea,
just quiet rooms and lighting low.
They tend to faces, hands, and skin
and send you out with extra glow.
clues: A calm little clinic where every treatment is about your skin.
North side of 9 Avenue in the 1400 block at the east end, number 1412, right next to a frozen-fruit-bowl spot.
Clean, spa-style signage; the first word means a brand-new bright star and begins with N.
stops.challenge: Find the word on the storefront that means 'feeling good' and photograph it.

stops.name: Shoe Closet (The)
stops.riddle:
They always come in twos, not ones,
stacked up in boxes, rows on rows.
Slip inside and take a walk;
the little mirror shows your toes.
clues: Everything sold here comes in pairs, and you try it on with your feet.
North side of 9 Avenue at the start of the 1400 block, number 1404, just east of 14 Street SE.
Walls of sneakers and comfort brands; the name pairs footwear with a place you store clothes, and starts with S.
stops.challenge: Photograph the smallest pair in the whole store.

stops.name: Canela
stops.riddle:
The smell of cinnamon drifts out,
of sugar, coffee, warm and sweet.
But not one crumb has milk or egg;
still every bite's a proper treat.
clues: A bake shop and cafe where nothing on the shelf comes from an animal.
South side of 9 Avenue in the 1300 block, number 1319, roughly opposite the Japanese blade shop.
The single-word name is Spanish for cinnamon, and it starts with C.
stops.challenge: Take a photo of the pastry with the most seeds or sprinkles on top.

stops.name: Knifewear
stops.riddle:
From far across the ocean came
the steel that all the cooks adore.
Hand-forged, honed, and wickedly sharp,
so mind your fingers near the door.
clues: Chefs come here for tools made by Japanese blacksmiths, and to get their edges put right again.
North side of 9 Avenue in the 1300 block, Unit 100A at number 1316, near the 13 Street SE end.
Rows of Japanese blades under glass plus a sharpening service; the one-word name starts with K.
stops.challenge: Photograph the longest blade on display, hands safely behind your back.

stops.name: Alberta Boot Company
stops.riddle:
Stitched-up leather, pointed toe,
a heel that clicks on wooden floor.
Handmade in Canada to last,
it's every cowboy's favourite store.
clues: Western footwear, handcrafted and made in Canada.
North side of 9 Avenue in the 1300 block, number 1312A, a couple of doors east of the Italian deli.
The name of the province is the very first word on the sign, so it starts with A.
stops.challenge: Find the tallest pair on display and photograph it next to your own shoes.

stops.name: Not Another Eye Store
stops.riddle:
Round or square, they perch on noses,
lenses polished, arms that fold.
Pick a pair and read the chart;
the smallest line is hard, we're told.
clues: If the street signs look blurry, this is the shop that sorts that out.
South side of 9 Avenue in the 1300 block, number 1321, a door or two from the vegan bake shop.
Frames line the walls in neat rows, and the cheeky name insists it is NOT one of these; it starts with N.
stops.challenge: Photograph the funniest pair of frames you can find.

stops.name: Tea Cult (The)
stops.riddle:
Dry leaves unfurl in steaming cups,
poured slow from something small and round.
Sit down, breathe in, and take your time;
there's hardly any seat around.
clues: Hot water, leaves from far away, and only a handful of seats. Slowness is the entire idea.
North side of 9 Avenue at the far east end, Unit 23 in the same 1420 complex as a popular brunch spot.
Tiny cups and shelves of tins, and the name puts the drink first; it starts with T.
stops.challenge: Photograph the tiniest teacup you can spot.

stops.name: Man Of Distinction
stops.riddle:
Blazers, brogues, and knotted ties,
all pre-loved but sharp and clean.
Someone wore them once before;
now they're waiting to be seen.
clues: Menswear that has already had one owner. It's consignment for gentlemen.
North side of 9 Avenue in the 1400 block at the east end, number 1416, a couple of doors past the acai spot.
Suits in the window, and the three-word name describes a very fine gentleman; it starts with M.
stops.challenge: Find the boldest necktie in the shop and photograph it.

stops.name: Change Is Good Cdc
stops.riddle:
Sweaters, jackets, cups and plates,
all second-hand and second-life.
The money doesn't stop at the till;
it helps a neighbour through some strife.
clues: A donation-fed second-hand shop whose profits go to a charity that helps people in recovery.
South side of 9 Avenue in the 1300 block, number 1317, next door west of the vegan bake shop.
Racks of pre-loved clothing plus goods from local makers; the name is a short phrase about transformation, starting with C.
stops.challenge: Find the most unusual mug or plate on the shelves and photograph it.

stops.name: Spolumbo's Fine Food & Deli
stops.riddle:
Sandwiches stacked as tall as bricks,
with sausage coiled behind the glass.
Framed sports jerseys watch you eat
while lineups out the doorway pass.
clues: An Italian deli known for its sausage and its enormous sandwiches.
North side of 9 Avenue at the west end of the 1300 block, number 1308, closest to 13 Street SE.
Canadian sports memorabilia covers the walls and there's a lunchtime lineup; the name starts with S and ends in an apostrophe-s.
stops.challenge: Count the sausage varieties in the cold case and photograph the strangest flavour.

stops.name: High Line Brewing
stops.riddle:
Steel tanks gleaming, hops in bags,
a taproom counter, glasses tall.
They make it here and pour it here;
just follow where the growlers call.
clues: Brewed on site and poured a few steps away. Bring ID.
North side of 9 Avenue in the 1300 block, Unit 113 inside the building at number 1318.
Look for the taproom entrance and the beer list on the board; the two-word name evokes an elevated railway and starts with H.
stops.challenge: Photograph the beer with the most creative name on the tap list.

stops.name: Imagine Vintage Wear
stops.riddle:
Bell-bottoms swing where the old decades hide,
With racks full of years stacked up side by side.
Try on a jacket somebody once wore —
A yesterday closet turned into a store.
clues: A clothing shop where every single item already had a first owner.
East end of the strip, south (odd-numbered) side of 9 Ave, in the 1300 block near 13 Street.
Two words starting with I and V: the first is what a famous John Lennon song asks you to do, the second means 'from an older era'.
stops.challenge: Find the outfit you think is the oldest thing in the shop and take a photo of it.

stops.name: Elysian Alchemy
stops.riddle:
Crystals that glitter and candles that glow,
And incense that curls where the quiet lamps go.
Seekers come looking for wonder and shine,
Where ordinary stones turn to something divine.
clues: A shop for crystals, incense and things a fortune-teller would love.
North (even-numbered) side of 9 Ave in the 1300 block, east end, right across from the vintage-shop stretch.
Two words starting with E and A; the second word is the old name for turning lead into gold.
stops.challenge: Find the biggest crystal in the shop and photograph it beside your hand for scale.

stops.name: Ama Jewellery & Watches
stops.riddle:
Tick-tock goes a tiny machine,
With gears smaller than crumbs on a plate.
Rings sparkle under the glass,
And time gets a fix while you wait.
clues: Sparkle in the display case, and something that ticks on your wrist.
South (odd-numbered) side of 9 Ave, deep in the 1300 block heading toward 14 Street.
A three-letter name beginning with A, followed by two words: one for gems, one for timepieces.
stops.challenge: Photograph a clock or watch face showing the exact minute you arrived.

stops.name: Barbie Nail And Massage
stops.riddle:
Ten little canvases painted with care,
Then shoulders unknotted while you sit in a chair.
Pick out a colour from bottles in rows,
And leave with a rainbow on fingers and toes.
clues: Ten tiny paint jobs — and a place to get the knots rubbed out afterwards.
South side of 9 Ave, in one of the units at number 1327, east end near 13 Street.
Starts with B and shares its name with the world's most famous doll.
stops.challenge: From the sidewalk, find and photograph the pinkest thing you can spot.

stops.name: Plant Terrariums & Garden Supplies
stops.riddle:
Tiny green worlds under bubbles of glass,
As mossy and small as a handful of grass.
Take home a jungle no bigger than bread —
Just give it some water and light overhead.
clues: Little gardens grown inside glass, plus the gear to keep green things alive.
South side of 9 Ave at number 1327, east end of the strip.
The name says exactly what it sells: a growing green thing, plus those sealed glass gardens.
stops.challenge: Photograph the smallest living plant you can find here.

stops.name: Recess
stops.riddle:
Paper and good pens and bright cards,
With stickers and gifts, small and neat.
Its name is the moment school stops
And everybody runs to the street.
clues: If you needed a birthday card, a notebook or a nice pen, this is your stop.
South side of 9 Ave in the 1300 block, a couple of doors east of number 1327.
One word beginning with R — it's what you call the break between classes.
stops.challenge: Find the funniest greeting card on the rack and photograph the front of it.

stops.name: Ami Tea Sub
stops.riddle:
A fat straw, a cold cup, dark pearls at the base,
And chewy wee bubbles you slurp at your pace.
A long crusty sandwich packed full to the end —
Sip something sweet while you wait with a friend.
clues: A drink you chew, and a sandwich you definitely don't.
The far east end of the strip, south side of 9 Ave, close to 14 Street.
Three short words: the first starts with A, the middle is a hot leafy drink, and the last is a kind of long sandwich.
stops.challenge: Photograph your drink with the fat straw in it, before the very first sip.

stops.name: Blooms On 9Th
stops.riddle:
Buckets of colour on long tidy stems,
With petals like ribbons and pollen like gems.
Wrapped up in paper and tied with a bow —
Somebody's day gets much better, you know.
clues: Everything sold here was grown and cut, and none of it will last the month.
The furthest east stop on the hunt — past 14 Street, in the 1400 block of 9 Ave.
Two words and a number: what flowers do, plus the name of the avenue you're standing on.
stops.challenge: Sniff around, then photograph the flower with the strongest smell.

stops.name: Inglewood Drive-In
stops.riddle:
Burgers and fries in a paper-wrapped stack,
And milkshakes so thick that the straw fights you back.
It's named for the way that the cars used to come —
Pull up, place an order, and lunchtime is done.
clues: Fast food the old-fashioned way: burgers, fries and shakes, no fancy dining room.
Not on the main avenue — head one block north and west, onto 12 Street between 8 and 9 Avenue.
Its name is this neighbourhood, plus the way you'd eat without ever leaving your car.
stops.challenge: Photograph the item on the menu board with the longest name.

stops.name: Rouge
stops.riddle:
A farmhouse from long before Calgary grew,
With gardens behind it where dinner-herbs grew.
Its one-word French name is a colour you know —
The same as a fire truck, a rose, or a bow.
clues: Fancy dinners served inside a very old house with a big garden around it.
One block north of the main strip, on 8 Avenue near 12 Street.
A single French word starting with R — it simply means 'red'.
stops.challenge: Take a photo of something growing in the garden outside.

stops.name: Supervariety
stops.riddle:
Piled-high sandwiches, crusty and fat,
And a corner-store name that's a little bit cheeky like that.
Two little words, and they both promise more —
A lunch that is bigger than lunches before.
clues: A sandwich spot with a name borrowed from an old-time corner shop.
South side of 9 Ave, sharing the number 1327 address with its neighbours, east end.
Starts with S: smash together a word meaning 'extra great' and a word meaning 'lots of different kinds'.
stops.challenge: Photograph the sandwich on the menu that lists the most ingredients.

stops.name: Blue Store (The)
stops.riddle:
Snacks by the till and a fridge humming low,
And shelves full of movies from decades ago.
You still rent a film here — imagine that! —
And the name is a colour, plain simple as that.
clues: Part corner store, part something almost every city has lost: a movie rental counter.
North (even-numbered) side of 9 Ave in the 1300 block, east end, opposite the odd-numbered shops.
The name is literally a colour plus the word 'store' — think sky, think ocean.
stops.challenge: Find a movie on the shelf that is older than you are and photograph the cover.

stops.name: Tibetan Trom
stops.riddle:
Prayer beads and statues and cloth painted bright,
With wool from the mountains where snow caps the height.
Gifts from a plateau the whole world calls high —
Step in, and the Himalayas feel nearby.
clues: Handmade crafts and gifts carried down from the world's tallest mountains.
South side of 9 Ave at number 1325, east end, sharing an address with a vintage-clothing shop.
The first word starts with T and names a famous Himalayan region; look for prayer beads and Buddha statues.
stops.challenge: Count the strings of prayer beads you can see, then photograph your favourite one.

stops.name: Dirty Duck
stops.riddle:
A pond-dwelling bird who has waded in muck
Pours pints for the grown-ups who stop for a while.
Two words in the name: one grimy, one fowl —
Nineteen and over may sit down and smile.
clues: A neighbourhood pub — pints, not lattes — and you need to be of legal age to go in.
North side of 9 Ave in the 1300 block, east end, a few doors west of the convenience store named after a colour.
Two words beginning with D: an adjective meaning 'not clean', and a bird that quacks.
stops.challenge: From the sidewalk, photograph the sign out front and count how many words on it start with D.

stops.name: Kent Of Inglewood
stops.riddle:
Brushes and blades and a lather of cream,
With straight-razor shaving brought back on the scene.
There's a chair for a trim and a shave to be had —
Exactly the shop that would please your grand-dad.
clues: Everything you'd need for a very old-fashioned shave, plus a barber's chair out back.
North side of 9 Ave at number 1316, west of 14 Street, sharing an address with a well-known knife shop.
The name is a man's first name starting with K, then the word 'of', then the name of this neighbourhood.
stops.challenge: Photograph the shaving brush you'd pick if you woke up tomorrow with a beard.

stops.name: Norley's Colombian Street Food
stops.riddle:
Corn cakes and pastries from far to the south,
Where coffee grows high and the Andes stretch out.
Street food served hot in a small friendly place —
One country's whole flavour packed onto a plate.
clues: South American street food from the country best known for coffee and emeralds.
North side of 9 Ave at number 1314, toward the west end of the 1300 block, right next to the shaving shop.
The first word is a person's name starting with N; the rest of the sign names the country and tells you the food is made for eating on the go.
stops.challenge: Photograph a menu item whose name you have never heard before.

stops.name: Tori Bar
stops.riddle:
Skewers of chicken set over the coals,
With smoke curling up as the charcoal glows red.
The name is the Japanese word for a bird —
And it hides round a corner, just off the main thread.
clues: Japanese grilled skewers, cooked over charcoal.
Not on 9 Ave itself — turn down 13 Street just south of the corner and look for it there.
Two short words; the first starts with T and is Japanese for 'bird'.
stops.challenge: Photograph the skewer you'd order, then count how many kinds are on the menu.
